front.title: Rego Policy Language for OAuth 2.0 Authorization

abstract.t: This specification defines how to use the Rego policy language in OAuth 2.0 authorization flows using Rich Authorization Requests (RAR). It defines the rego_policy authorization data type for carrying policy proposals in authorization_details, enabling fine-grained, dynamic authorization decisions that go beyond traditional scope-based access control.

section.title: Introduction
section.t: Traditional OAuth 2.0 authorization relies on static scopes to define access permissions. While scopes work well for coarse-grained access control, they are insufficient for scenarios requiring dynamic, context-aware authorization decisions—particularly in AI agent systems where the permitted operations may depend on runtime conditions such as transaction amounts, time windows, or resource attributes.

This specification extends OAuth 2.0 to support the Rego policy language, as used by Open Policy Agent (OPA). Rego enables expressive, declarative policies that can encode complex authorization rules. By integrating Rego into OAuth flows, this specification enables:

ul.li: Clients to propose fine-grained operation policies in authorization requests;
Authorization Servers to validate, register, and reference policies;
Resource Servers to enforce policies at runtime using OPA.

section.title: Requirements Language
section.t: The key words "MUST", "MUST NOT", "REQUIRED", "SHALL", "SHALL NOT", "SHOULD", "SHOULD NOT", "RECOMMENDED", "NOT RECOMMENDED", "MAY", and "OPTIONAL" in this document are to be interpreted as described in BCP 14 when, and only when, they appear in all capitals.

section.title: Applicability
section.t: This specification is designed to work with Rich Authorization Requests (RAR) as the primary mechanism for carrying policy proposals. The rego_policy authorization data type MAY be used with various OAuth 2.0 authorization flows, including but not limited to:

ul.li: Authorization Code Grant (with or without PAR);
Client Credentials Grant;
Token Exchange ;
Resource Owner Password Credentials Grant.

section.t: Different authorization flows may have different security considerations when using policy proposals. Implementations SHOULD carefully evaluate the security implications discussed in Section 7 based on their specific deployment scenario.

section.title: RAR Integration
section.t: This specification defines the rego_policy authorization data type for use with Rich Authorization Requests (RAR) . The policy proposal is carried within the authorization_details parameter as the primary mechanism.
Key aspects of the RAR integration:

ul.li: Authorization Data Type: The rego_policy type is registered in the RAR Authorization Data Types registry (Section 9.4 of RFC 9396). It contains the policy content, entry point, and optional context.

Token Response: The access token includes a policy_ref claim referencing the registered policy. Per RFC 9396 Section 7.1, the token response MAY include enriched authorization information such as the full policy content.

Complementary Use: RAR enables structured authorization requests with type-specific details, while Rego Policy enables expressive, Turing-complete policy definitions. Implementations MAY combine rego_policy with other RAR types.

section.t: Implementations SHOULD ensure consistency between authorization_details requirements and Rego policy evaluations. The Authorization Server MAY use RAR types to determine applicable policy templates or validation rules.

dl.dd: A declarative policy language designed for Open Policy Agent (OPA). Rego policies define rules that evaluate to allow or deny decisions based on input data.
A general-purpose policy engine that evaluates Rego policies against structured input data.
A framework defined in RFC 9396 for expressing fine-grained authorization requirements through the authorization_details parameter.
An authorization data type for RAR that carries a Rego policy proposal within the authorization_details parameter.
An identifier for a policy that has been validated and registered by the Authorization Server, included in access tokens via the policy_ref claim.

section.title: RAR Authorization Data Type
section.t: This specification defines the rego_policy authorization data type for use with Rich Authorization Requests (RAR).

section.title: rego_policy
section.t: The rego_policy authorization data type carries a Rego policy within the authorization_details parameter. It enables clients to propose fine-grained authorization policies as part of the authorization request.

dl.dd: rego_policy
Object
authorization_details (RFC 9396)

section.title: Structure
section.t: The rego_policy authorization data type has the following fields:

dl.dd: REQUIRED. The authorization data type identifier. MUST be "rego_policy" for this specification.
REQUIRED. An object containing the Rego policy definition.
OPTIONAL. An object providing structured input data for policy evaluation. This data is passed to OPA as the input object.

section.t: The policy object has the following fields:

dl.dd: REQUIRED. The policy language type. MUST be "rego" for this specification. Future extensions MAY define additional types.
REQUIRED (if uri not present). The Rego policy as a string. The policy MUST be syntactically valid Rego.
OPTIONAL. A URI reference to an externally hosted policy. If provided, the AS MAY fetch the policy from this location.
REQUIRED. The rule name that serves as the policy entry point. For authorization decisions, this MUST be "allow".

section.title: Policy Requirements
section.t: Rego policies used with this specification MUST adhere to the following requirements:

ol.li: Entry Point: The policy MUST define an allow rule as the entry point. This rule MUST evaluate to a boolean value.
Package Declaration: The policy MUST include a package declaration. The recommended package name is "agent" or a domain-specific namespace.
Default Deny: The policy SHOULD include default allow = false to ensure deny-by-default behavior.
Input Reference: The policy accesses context data via the input object, which is populated from the context field of the rego_policy authorization data type.

section.title: policy_ref Claim
section.t: The policy_ref claim is included in access tokens to reference a policy that has been validated and registered by the Authorization Server.

dl.dd: policy_ref
Object
Access tokens
REQUIRED. A unique identifier for the registered policy, assigned by the Authorization Server.
OPTIONAL. The version of the policy. Useful for policy updates.

OPTIONAL. A cryptographic hash of the policy content using the format algorithm-base64value (e.g., "sha256-..."). When present, the Resource Server MUST verify that the fetched policy content matches this hash before evaluating the policy. This prevents tampering with policy content during transmission.
OPTIONAL. A URL where the Resource Server can fetch the full policy content if needed.

section.title: Policy Context
section.t: The context field within rego_policy provides structured input data for policy evaluation. This data is passed to OPA as the input object.
The context structure is flexible and can include any attributes relevant to policy evaluation. Common categories include:

ul.li: user: User identity and attributes;
agent: Agent identity, platform, instance, and client metadata;
resource: Target resource attributes;
action: Requested action details;
environment: Contextual conditions (time, location, channel, language, device fingerprint).

section.t: See Section 3.1 for an example of context within the authorization_details structure.

ol.li: Authorization Request: Client sends authorization request with authorization_details containing an object of type rego_policy, with policy and optional context fields. This leverages RAR (RFC 9396) for structured authorization requests.
Syntax Validation: AS validates that the Rego policy is syntactically correct and safe to execute.
Policy Evaluation: AS evaluates the policy against the request context to determine authorization scope. This may involve checking user consent requirements and policy constraints.

Token Response: AS issues access token with policy_ref claim referencing the registered policy. Per RFC 9396 Section 7.1, the token response MAY include enriched authorization information in additional JSON fields (e.g., policy containing the full policy content) alongside the access token.
API Request: Client presents token to Resource Server.
Policy Fetch: RS retrieves the policy via policy_ref from AS (if not cached). The policy may have been returned directly in the enriched token response.
Policy Evaluation: RS sends policy and request input to OPA for evaluation.
Enforcement: RS enforces OPA's allow/deny decision.
Response: RS returns result to client.

section.title: Reverse-Guided Authorization
section.t: Traditional OAuth error responses indicate authorization failure without providing guidance on how to obtain valid authorization. In AI agent scenarios, where agents may need to autonomously navigate authorization requirements, resource servers can provide structured guidance that enables agents to construct appropriate authorization requests.

section.title: Error Response Format
section.t: When an agent's request lacks sufficient authorization, the resource server returns an HTTP 403 Forbidden response with a JSON body containing a rego_profile object. This object provides machine-readable guidance on the required authorization conditions.

figure.name: Reverse-Guided Authorization Error Response

section.title: Rego Profile Structure
section.t: The rego_profile object contains the following fields:

dl.dd: REQUIRED. URI of the policy profile document that defines the authorization requirements for this resource.
OPTIONAL. Array of scope values that the access token MUST include.
OPTIONAL. Array of claim names that MUST be present in the token.
OPTIONAL. Object defining policy constraints that MUST be satisfied. Each constraint specifies the data type, description, and whether it is required.
OPTIONAL. Boolean indicating whether user consent is required. If true, the agent MUST obtain explicit user approval.
OPTIONAL. Boolean indicating whether authorization evidence recording is required.
REQUIRED. Identifier of the authorization server capable of issuing tokens that satisfy these requirements.
REQUIRED. URL of the token endpoint where the agent can request appropriate authorization.

section.title: Agent Adaptive Behavior
section.t: Upon receiving a reverse-guided authorization response, the AI agent SHOULD:

ol.li: Parse the rego_profile to understand authorization requirements.
Verify that the specified auth_server is trusted before proceeding.
Construct a new authorization request including required scopes, policy proposal satisfying constraints, and appropriate policy context.
If confirmation_required is true, initiate user consent flow.
Submit the authorization request to the specified token_endpoint.

section.t: This adaptive approach enables agents to "learn" authorization requirements dynamically, reducing the need for pre-programmed knowledge of each resource server's policies.

section.title: Security Considerations
section.t: Implementations of reverse-guided authorization MUST consider the following security aspects:

ul.li: Auth Server Verification: Agents MUST verify that the auth_server specified in the rego_profile is trusted before submitting authorization requests. Blindly following redirects could lead to credential theft.

Constraint Validation: Agents SHOULD validate that constraint values are reasonable before including them in authorization requests. Malicious resource servers might attempt to induce agents to request excessive permissions.

Information Disclosure: The rego_profile reveals authorization requirements, which is acceptable as it only exposes "what is needed" not "why it is needed." This is analogous to OAuth scope definitions.
TLS Protection: All communications MUST use TLS to prevent man-in-the-middle attacks on the error response.

section.title: Policy Validation
section.t: Upon receiving a policy_proposal, the AS MUST perform the following validation steps:

ol.li: Syntax Check: Parse the Rego policy and verify it is syntactically valid.
Entry Point Check: Verify the policy defines an allow rule.
Safety Check: Ensure the policy does not contain dangerous operations (e.g., infinite loops, external HTTP calls in restricted environments).
Scope Check: Optionally verify the policy does not exceed the client's registered permissions.

section.title: Policy Registration
section.t: After validation, the AS registers the policy:

ol.li: Assign a unique policy identifier;
Store the policy content (or reference);
Associate the policy with the authorization session;
Optionally, pre-compile the policy for faster evaluation.

section.t: If policy validation fails, the AS MUST return an error:

section.title: Policy Retrieval
section.t: When the RS receives an access token with a policy_ref claim, it retrieves the policy using one of the following methods:

ul.li: Fetch from AS: Use the endpoint URL in the policy_ref to retrieve the policy.
Local Cache: Use a cached copy if available and not expired.
Introspection: Include policy content in token introspection response.

section.t: The RS evaluates the policy using OPA:

section.title: Enforcement Decision
section.t: Based on OPA's response:

ul.li: If result is true: Allow the operation;
If result is false: Deny with 403 Forbidden;
If evaluation fails: Deny with 500 Internal Server Error.

section.title: Applicability to Different Authorization Flows
section.t: The policy proposal mechanism defined in this specification is designed to be flexible and applicable to various OAuth 2.0 authorization flows. This section provides examples for common use cases beyond PAR.

section.title: Authorization Code Grant (without PAR)
section.t: When using traditional authorization code grant without PAR, the policy proposal and policy_context SHOULD be included in a JWT using the "request" parameter as defined in [RFC9101]. This mechanism, known as JWT-Secured Authorization Request (JAR), is specifically designed for redirect-based flows and provides integrity protection while maintaining consistency with the PAR mechanism.

figure.artwork: GET /authorize? response_type=code& client_id=spiffe://agent.example/agent& request=eyJhbGciOiJSUzI1NiIsImtpZCI6ImFnZW50LWtleSJ9..signature& state=xyz123 HTTP/1.1 Host: as.example.com

section.t: The JWT payload (decoded) contains:
Using the JWT request parameter provides the following benefits:

ul.li: Integrity Protection: The JWT signature prevents tampering with the policy proposal and context;
Privacy: Policy content is not exposed in URLs, server logs, or browser history;
Consistency: Same structure as PAR, just different transport mechanism;
No Length Limits: Avoids URL length restrictions that affect query parameters.

section.t: Implementations MUST validate the JWT signature before processing the policy proposal. The client's public key can be obtained through pre-registration or dynamic client registration.

section.title: Security Considerations by Flow
section.t: Different authorization flows have different security characteristics when using RAR with rego_policy:

dl.dd: authorization_details is transmitted in the PAR request body with JWT signature protection. Provides integrity and confidentiality. Highest security for policy proposals.
When using JWT-Secured Authorization Request (JAR, RFC 9101), authorization_details is protected by the JWT signature. Implementations MUST validate the JWT before processing.
Direct AS communication with TLS; standard client authentication usually sufficient. authorization_details is in the request body.
Similar security to Client Credentials; ensure policy binding to the exchanged token subject.

section.t: General security requirements for all flows:

ul.li: Integrity Protection: authorization_details SHOULD be signed when transmitted through untrusted channels (e.g., browser redirects). Use JAR or PAR for protection.
Length Considerations: Rego policies may be large. Implementations SHOULD use PAR or JAR to avoid URL length limitations.
RAR Type Validation: AS MUST validate that the type field is "rego_policy" and reject unknown types.

section.title: Policy Injection
section.t: Rego policies submitted by clients are executable code. The AS MUST:

ul.li: Validate policy syntax before registration;
Execute policies in sandboxed environments;
Limit policy execution time and resource usage;
Restrict dangerous built-in functions (e.g., http.send).

section.title: Policy Scope Escalation
section.t: Clients MUST NOT be able to propose policies that exceed their registered permissions. The AS SHOULD maintain policy templates or scope hierarchies to enforce this.

section.title: Policy Integrity
section.t: The policy_ref in access tokens MUST reference policies stored securely by the AS. Resource Servers MUST fetch policies only from trusted sources.

section.title: RAR Authorization Data Type Registration
section.t: This specification registers the following authorization data type in the "OAuth Authorization Data Types" registry established by RFC 9396:

A Rego policy for fine-grained authorization decisions, including policy content, entry point, and optional evaluation context.
